_about: One geometry for the two sister marks: Vitals' plan ring and Gauge's reading ring.
The same file lives in both repos (Vitals design/brand/mark-geometry.json, Gauge docs/design-concepts/mark-geometry.json);
edit one, copy it to the other, and run both generators (Vitals: pnpm brand; Gauge: docs/design-concepts/gauge-mark.py).
Units are the 24-unit design space, centre 12,12. Every ring has its outer edge at `outer` (ring radius = outer - stroke / 2),
round caps, and the same stroke, hairline and dot sizes in both marks at every tier. Only the identity differs:
Vitals: ivory ring open at four o'clock, the hairline bezel across the opening, a gold dot inside aimed at it.
Gauge: a gold reading arc over 70% of the circle from 12 o'clock on the dim track, an ivory dot where the reading ends.

adaptive._note: Launcher foreground, themed icon, legacy mipmaps (the 72 dp window): ring edge 29.85 dp; nothing past 32.9 dp.

notification._note: White silhouette. Its own smaller ring (outer 9.4) so Gauge's end dot keeps the 2 dp padding; Vitals uses the same ring.

inapp._note: In-app and web marks: the 24-unit space as is (Vitals' RingMark crops it to 2 2 20).

tiers._note: Pick by rendered size in px (CSS px, dp): small <= small_max_px, medium <= medium_max_px, else standard.

small._note: No hairline at 24 px and under: a sub-pixel line only muddies the ring.

mono._note: One colour, alpha only. The main stroke stays full weight (a touch heavier), the track is a hairline at half alpha, the dot grows.

themed._note: Android 13+ themed icon and Vitals' PWA monochrome icon.

notification._note: Ring edge 9.4 so Gauge's end dot (8.4 + 1.6) stops at 10: the 2 dp padding.

vitals._note: The opening faces bisector_deg (clockwise from 3 o'clock); the dot sits on that line, dot_at from the centre, clear inside the ring.

gauge._note: The reading runs clockwise from start_deg (12 o'clock) over `reading` of the circle; the dot is centred on the ring where it stops.
